summary: Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi (~1933–1936). He held posts at Kyoto University, Nagoya University (1955–1977), University of Hamburg (1964), and Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–1984).

Yoshito S. Hakeda (1924–1983) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served at Columbia University, where he was a Professor in 1966 and an Associate Professor of Japanese and Religion until 1983.
Yoshitoyo Ohara specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshitsugu Sawai (b. 1951) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under supervisors including John B. Carman, he served as a professor and Dean of Humanities at Tenri University (~1984–2017).
Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions at Taisho University (attested 1998–2026) and Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe (b. 1947), active in computational fields and Tibetology, earned a Dr. in Science at Tohoku University (1975). He was a Senior Research Fellow there (1975–2012, 2018) and held visiting or concurrent professorships at Berkeley, JAIST, and NII.

Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939). He later served as a Professor at Rissho University (~1950–1987) and director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (~1975–1987).

Yosuke Fujimoto works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and was a Research Fellow at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (2025–2026).

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, and held posts at CUHK (attested 1999) and Rowan University (attested 2007–2018).
Youwei Kang (1858–1927) was a scholar in philosophy and sinology. He founded Wanmu Caotang in 1890 and served there from around 1891 to 1898, teaching students including Qichao Liang.

Yozo Taniyama (b. 1972) works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tohoku University (~1991–1996), he held positions at Shitennoji University (~2003–2007), St. Thomas University, Japan (~2007–2010), Sophia University (~2010–2012), and Tohoku University (~2012).

Yrjö Moses Jalmari Biese (1903–1983) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Helsinki under J. N. Reuter. He held academic posts at the University of Helsinki (1932–1950) and served as Professor of English at the University of Turku (1946–1967).

Yu Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Liu studied at HKBU, UIC, and the University of Hong Kong (MA 2024), and held posts as a research assistant at UIC (2021–2024) and editor at Hong Kong Ta Kung Wen Wei Media Group (2024).
Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed master's study under Chün-fang Yü at Columbia University and studied under doctoral supervisor Natasha Heller (attested 2018), as well as traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-Yin Hsu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Hsu earned a Ph.D. from the National University of Singapore (2014–2019) and held a post in the Faculty of East Asian Studies at Ruhr University Bochum in 2022.

Yu-kwan Ng (b. 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at CUHK and McMaster University (Ph.D. ~1980–1985), he held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~2001–2006).

Yu-min Lee is a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington. Lee held a post as a Professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).
Yuan Ren is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who completed a PhD at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 1998).

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Gongga Rinpoche and held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and as a researcher at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism.
